newsitem.title: USA: Illinois Central may not meet EPS estimates.
newsitem.headline: Illinois Central may not meet EPS estimates.

text.p: Illinois Central Corp said Wednesday it may not meet analysts' fourth quarter earnings estimates, citing lower than expected grain movement.

"To put the fourth quarter into perspective, the first, second and third quarters came in at $0.54, $0.51 and $0.52, respectively," Hunter Harrison, president and chief executive of the railroad holding company, said in a statement.

"We anticipate that the fourth quarter, excluding our previously announced non-recurring gain, will equal or exceed any of the prior quarters but may not live up to the Street's expectations, given grain movements since harvest," he said.
According to First Call, the consensus of analysts' earnings estimates for fourth quarter was $0.66 a share versus $0.53 last year.
In October, Illinois Central said it sold its investment in an insurance company, which will result in a one-time gain of about $0.07 a share which is not generally reflected in analysts' estimates.
The company had said earlier that fourth quarter earnings would depend on grain volumes.

"The good news is that the grain elevators in our service territories in Illinois and Iowa are full," Harrison said. "It becomes a timing issue of when the grain will move. We had originally expected more it to move in this quarter."
Illinois Central's principal freight railroad subsidiaries are the Illinois Central; the Chicago, Central & Pacific; and the Cedar River.
